title.narrative: Sustainable Colombia Facility - IDB Trust Fund

description.narrative:
Sveriges ambassad har hängivet stöttat Colombias ansträngningar för att uppnå fred i över två årtionden. Som ett resultat av fredsavtalet med FARC, och som svar på de punkter som fastställts genom avtalet, har Colombias regering upprättat en strategi för postkonflikten vid namn Colombia en Paz. Denna strategi består av fyra fonder som etablerats med syfte att dra största möjliga nytta av det internationella utvecklingssamarbetet i landet. Sverige stöder de fyra fonderna. Världsbankens Trust Fond fokuserar på att tillämpa lagen om konfliktens offer (kollektiv gottgörelse) och innefattar ett särskilt avsnitt om tekniskt stöd till ett pilotprojekt inom lantmäteri; FN:s Multi-partner Trust Fund (MPTF) intar ett kortsiktigt perspektiv och åtar strategier för snabba svarsåtgärder; EU:s Trust Fund (EUTF) är en fond med medellångt tidsperspektiv och landsbygdsutveckling som huvudfokus.
Den fjärde fonden, Interamerikanska utvecklingsbankens (IDB) Sustainable Colombia Facility, väntas komplettera de övriga fonderna för postkonflikten genom att främja långsiktiga mål som integrerar social, ekonomisk och miljömässig utveckling i konfliktdrabbade regioner.
Sustainable Colombia Facility söker åtgärda fyra huvudsakliga och sammanlänkade utmaningar: (i) skogsskövling och förlust av naturkapital; (ii) fattigdom på landsbygd och regional utveckling; (iii) bristande institutionell kapacitet och samordning på lokal nivå; och (iv) klimatrelaterade utmaningar. Dessutom väntas initiativet stödja genomförandet av de Globala målen för hållbar utveckling och Colombias nationella bidrag (Intended Nationally Determined Contributions; INDC) till dessa. Fonden prioriterar geografiska områden och provinser som är strategiska för landsbygdsutveckling, miljöskydd och fredsbyggande insatser.

This contribution to a multi-donor funding mechanisms is for a Trust Fund designed to implement Colombia’s Peace Agreement with FARC. The contribution’s objective is to support projects and programmes aimed at maximizing the environmental, economic, and social dividends of peace in Colombia, primarily in territories at the intersection of armed conflict incidence, strategic areas for sustainable rural development and environmental conservation. For this purpose, this facility addresses five objectives: (i) Promoting conservation and sustainable use of biodiversity; (ii) Forging and support sustainable rural development; (iii) Supporting the implementation of national policies that promote climate change mitigation and reduction of deforestation; (iv) Supporting capacity building in areas affected by the armed conflict; and (v) Mainstreaming climate change considerations in the development agenda as a cross-sectoral topic.

The Sustainable Colombia Fund is part of the Colombia in Peace strategy for post-conflict and is one of the four trust funds created for the implementation of the Peace Agreement with FARC; specifically with regards to the first component of the Agreement: The Comprehensive Rural Reform.
The main outcome of the Fund is to maximize the environmental, economic, and social dividends of peace in Colombia, primarily in territories at the intersection of armed conflict incidence, strategic areas for sustainable rural development and environmental conservation.
The Fund is initially established for a period of 15 years and will provide medium-term and long-term support to the post-conflict in Colombia.
The specific objectives of the Fund are: (i) to promote conservation and sustainable use of biodiversity; (ii) to forge and support sustainable rural development; (iii) to support the implementation of national policies that promote climate change mitigation and reduction of deforestation; (iv) to support capacity building in areas affected by the armed conflict; and (v) to mainstream climate change considerations in the development agenda as a cross-sectoral topic.

description.narrative:
This Trust Fund has faced numerous challenges since the signing of its agreement, mainly related to delays in both its definition and implementation. Nevertheless, the Fund has managed to finance 27 projects of high relevance for peace-building and the generation of sustainable development activities in areas long affected by the conflict in Colombia.
Among the overall results achieved until 2024, the following should be highlighted:
- Ecological conservation processes reached a total of 522,340 hectares covered. These processes included more than 350 conservation agreements with local communities and 19 bioeconomy initiatives.
- The sustainable agriculture processes reached a total of 208,959 hectares covered. The processes enabled productive development for local communities, including the strengthening of 22 value chains, 6 zero deforestation agreements and 40 commercial agreements.
- By 2024, 11 projects were implemented to support and strengthen public institutions at national and local levels. These projects included the design and implementation of 10 information systems, 3 annual deforestation reports, 2 training programs and 2 financial instruments.
- The implementation of the 27 projects has impacted the quality of life of the community by:
* Improving the income of 748 small producers by creating opportunities for economic diversification and guaranteeing environmental sustainability and adaptability to climate change in PDET municipalities.
*Strengthening the productive and conservation capacities of 687 producers to carry out productive transformations in seven projects in Bolívar, Antioquia and Nariño.
*Implementing a comprehensive training strategy to improve the level of technical knowledge in sustainable production, climate change adaptation measures, and commercial linkages for the production lines of cocoa, coffee, beekeeping, livestock, bananas, and fish farming.
*Implementing the Dialogue and Coordination Strategy for the reduction of deforestation and forest management, maintaining relationships with national and local representatives of indigenous groups.
*Developing of action plans associated with the restoration program, control of deforestation, and forest management in the territories of indigenous groups, in addition to activities related to the strengthening of self-government and the traditional knowledge of indigenous groups.
*Implementing the Comprehensive Technical Assistance (ATI) strategy to strengthen the capacities of farmers and indigenous communities in the Paramillo and Catatumbo Barí Natural National Parks (PNN).
*Signing of 60 use and conservation agreements between PNN and 69 farming families with individual enterprises in the Paramillo PNN, and progress is being made in the signing of 23 additional agreements, covering a total of 919.5 hectares distributed in areas of conservation, restoration, and sustainable production systems.
*Signing individual and collective ATI agreements with 459 families to strengthen environmental, productive, social, and entrepreneurial capacities in the development of sustainable, productive enterprises and conservation and restoration actions.
*Developing instruments to strengthen the capacities of communities, forestry initiatives, and environmental authorities in sustainable forest management and forest governance.
*Strengthening the productive, environmental, social, commercial and entrepreneurial capacities of six community-based farmer and indigenous associations for the development of value chains.
More generally, the following are also results of the Fund during the period:
- The IDB, together with the UTC, submitted the audit report for 2023. The auditor's opinion was unmodified, meaning that the financial statements were presented fairly in all material respects, and was therefore accepted by Sida without any comments.
- Following the recommendations of the 2022 Mid-Term Evaluation in terms of strengthening links with partners and other entities in the field and active participation in key events, the Fund actively participated in the Conference of the Parties to the Convention on Biological Diversity (COP 16) held in Cali.
- The UTC coordinated several side events in Cali during COP 16, involving different partners from civil society, NGOs, national and local public institutions and donors. These panels made visible the good results of the projects implemented by the Fund by sharing the experiences of some of the beneficiaries, who were invited as panellists in all the events. Sida participated in one of these panels and accompanied others.
- A new Multi-Annual Investment Plan (PPI) for the period 2024-2026 was presented following a new contribution of USD 10 million from Norway. The Biodiversity Action Plan launched during COP 16 is the main policy framework to be implemented through this PPI.
- Only one Technical Committee and one Steering Committee took place in 2024. These committees evaluated and approved the new PPI, which will be funded by Norway's new contribution and the remaining funds from previous disbursements that haven't been allocated or implemented.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
